summary: Assessed materially in line with the national position, with one documented data caveat. no region-specific incident, ordinance or enforcement finding was identified in the dedicated country dossier for this region; no sub-national facility, expression or assembly restriction exists anywhere in the country, and the 2023 national trans-equality law's implementation (including its education-facing parts) falls to the regional government. The national victimisation baseline applies here: a 2026 federation report found 44% of LGTBI respondents had experienced a hate-motivated incident. Uniquely, this region records the LOWEST per-capita hate-offence rate in the country; the dossier stresses that the region has no regional LGTBI law of its own and runs no monitoring observatory, so the low recorded count reflects the absence of counting infrastructure and must not be read as evidence of protection.

sources.summary: Official state-gazette text of Law 4/2023, of 28 February, for the real and effective equality of trans people and the guarantee of the rights of LGTBI people (published 1 March 2023, 63 pages, reference BOE-A-2023-5366): the national trans-equality law whose administrative and education-facing provisions are implemented by the autonomous communities - the framework this region applies.

International human-rights organisation news release (16 February 2023) welcoming the country's new gender-recognition law: legal gender recognition by self-declaration from age 12 under certain conditions without medical diagnosis, placing the country among autonomy-first jurisdictions (with Argentina, Belgium, Colombia, Denmark, Ireland, Luxembourg, Malta, Norway, Portugal, Uruguay); frames diagnostic and sterilisation requirements elsewhere as rights violations.

Criminal-defence law-firm analysis (June 2026, updated September 2026) disentangling three frequently conflated statutes: the 2023 trans-equality law is an ordinary statute that never amended the criminal code (its content is civil, administrative, health, employment and educational); the discrimination aggravating factor and the hate-offences provisions in the criminal code come from a 2022 reform (hate offences: 1 to 4 years' imprisonment plus a 6-12 month fine); 'gender expression' appears in no article of the criminal code.
